title: Abstract skeleton: headings, word budget, what each section must establish
outcome: A skeleton Aarav fills in himself: problem -> fix -> why it matters, with a word budget and the points each section must land
acceptance: Section headings in the organisers' order (problem -> fix -> why it matters, plus limits) with a word budget per section totalling 850-950, under the 1,000 cap
Under each heading: bullet notes (fragments, max ~12 words each) of what must be established, each tagged to a fact-card row, guardrail or term; zero full sentences of abstract prose (Charter)
Reflects D1 layered headline, D2 METR wording, D3 one credited Airlock clause, D12 hero scenario, D13 numbers-as-targets
summary:
abstract/SKELETON.md: 4 sections in the organisers' order (1 Problem 300 = gap 70 / blunt tools fail 110 / what exists 120; 2 Fix 330 = IBAN example 40 / mediated path 70 / identify 45 / contain 60 / recover 75 / audit 40; 3 Why it matters 170; 4 Limits + will-show 85) + title 15 = 900 words. ~125 note bullets, each <=12 words, no sentences, tagged to fact-card rows, P/F/W/L/X ids and TERMS words.
D1: opens on the dependency gap; provenance named in 2b; 'selective undo' as the 2e payoff only; testimony vs evidence in 3a. D2: METR = blunt stop failed, card #1 qualifiers, never-quote items. D3: Airlock box (what the one clause must convey + forbidden comparisons; one mention only). D12: F2+ running example in 2a. D13: our numbers = definitions + targets (R/C/post-alert/irreversible/re-emitted = 0); TTI/TTC are definitions only.
Also: title keyword combos (no finished titles), a 5-step writing plan (Fix first → Problem → Why → Limits → title; GUARDRAILS §4 + TERMS Ctrl-F; save as abstract/DRAFT-R1.md and log on ABS-07). Flags carried in: #7 'dense spread' misplacement (ABS-01 changes) and card #1 overriding GUARDRAILS P2.
review:
[panel · changes] CHANGES: 2 must-fix, both cheap. Structure passes. The order is problem -> fix -> why -> limits; budgets total 900 and every subsection sums correctly. D1 is layered as decided (gap 1a, provenance 2b, selective undo 2e only, testimony vs evidence 3a, flagged for Aarav). D2: 1b uses card #1/#2 qualifiers and the never-quote items. D3: the box gives one credited clause, P5's journal point goes inside it or unnamed, and the 'dense spread' fix is carried. D12: F2+ with the W6 label and x10 kept out of the story. D13: definitions + targets, no seconds. Cross-checks against FACT-CARD, GUARDRAILS v2, TERMS and C6 v2 are clean: 'never cancelled here' in 2d vs cancel_outbox in 2e is correct.
PASTEABLE-PROSE CHECK: PASS. No bullet is a sentence. The quoted strings ('tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head', 'orthogonal rollback', 'maps to', 'in a safe state') are mandated wording or attributed quotations, not prose. The writing-plan sentences are instructions. The residual risk is structural: ~124 bullets in a fixed order invite one sentence per bullet, which reads kit-shaped and machine-like. Must-fix 1 also addresses that.
MUST-FIX 1: the budget cannot hold the points. 1c has 12 bullets plus a 7-bullet box in 120 words, and the clause alone is 20-30. 2d has 10 in 60, 2e has 12 in 75, 2f has 7 in 40. Every line reads as 'must establish', so Aarav either overruns or writes telegraphic text, and both hurt with this jury. Tag every bullet MUST or IF-ROOM, at most ~1 MUST per 15 budget words. Demote these to IF-ROOM: 1b #9 catalogued incidents (keep 'single-agent, in our search' only as a qualifier) and #3 hindsight; 1c sagas #13, OTel #11, FAMAS #6, random baseline #5; the box's optional #7 numbers (delete them: they cannot fit in 30 words beside 'by design', 'orthogonal rollback', 'complementary' and the arXiv ID); 2b MCP #12; 2d epoch and anti-framing; 2e append-only, over-taint (L2 covers it) and the dry-run chain (keep 'approved plan'); 2f tamper-alert freeze. Define TTI/TTC once, in 3b: delete the duplicates in 2c/2d. Add one line under the budget table: section totals are binding; subsections are +/-15 and bullet order inside a subsection is free. ABS-07 reviewers then enforce totals, not micro-budgets.
MUST-FIX 2: the framing can be sharper. The jury 'rewards the team that frames the problem best'. Our strongest frame is that the brief's own requirement ('reverses one agent's damage WITHOUT discarding the other agents' work') is undefined once honest agents have read the bad write. 1a states that abstractly, and the IBAN example only arrives in 2a, inside the fix. Move the example into 1a so the gap is shown, not told. 1a bullets: brief's frame + brief's 'without discarding' clause [CHARTER] -> crm swaps IBAN; billing/payments/comms acted on it; inventory/docs untouched [D12 · W6 label] -> their work is honest AND built on the bad write -> 'undo crm' undefined [P1]. Rebudget: 1a 70->100, 1b 110->90, 1c 120->110 (problem stays 300). Delete 2a: 2b opens by walking the example. Then 2b 70->80, 2d 60->65, 2e 75->95, 2f 40->45 (fix stays 330, total 900). Also show in 2c/2d/2e that they map 1:1 to the brief's three scores (time-to-identify / time-to-contain / clean recovery). That is already the structure; one tag line per heading makes it explicit.
SHOULD-FIX: 3a, tag the brief's 'an agent that can be audited, not only demoed' [CHARTER]; testimony vs evidence answers it directly. 3b, add a bullet: the brief's three scores have no agreed measurement in the standards we checked -> we define checkable ones, scored against the oracle [RES-08 headline; qualifier 'in the standards we checked']. Ask zoya to add it to GUARDRAILS as W7 if adopted.
Nits: 1b, '✗ internal / cyber [#1]' is enough; the 'card #1 overrides P2' flag is stale because P2 is fixed in ABS-02 v2. 2d, write 'reconciliation mismatch (class U)', not bare 'class U' (D7). 3c, NIST MANAGE 4.3 is sourced in RES-08 [19], not on the card; tag it there. Re-review is quick once the tags and the 1a move are in.
